It's what happens when you are starving to death. It's debatable which phase can be called "starvation mode", as the body goes through several stages to survive actual starvation. But, it's generally agreed that a person can't enter anything like starvation mode until they've gone at least 3 days with absolutely no food, or many days with very little food.

In basic, it's the point where the body changes its metabolic strategy. It realizes that new food won't be coming in to the stomach, so instead it starts consuming itself. After a week with no food, your body will consume your own muscles to produce the energy that your vital organs need.

Very fat people can go much, much longer with no food. The record is 380 days - though that person was medically supervised and given supplements of vitamins and minerals.

The body is very, very good at energy management. Evolution has been perfecting the strategy since life started. Your metabolism is so good that it will outlive you by several weeks. I kid you not; the internal decay of a dead body is conducted by that person's metabolism.

I'm excited that Voat has a burgeoning coffee sub and I'm hoping that this shapes up to be as content-driven as /r/coffee. What is everyone's thoughts on turning /v/coffee towards a content and info-dense direction? I understand that some people might find that orientation too snobby and serious. On the other hand, the semi-serious nature of /r/coffee helped me become the awesome barista I am by directly introducing me to over-obsessive coffee making. A separate subverse for snobs is an option but I think it can be helpful for people new to coffee to be exposed to the over-obsessive.

To clarify what I mean by content and info-dense: no image-only posts, discussion-oriented, lots of questions.

Introduce us to coffee from around the world, the science of coffee, the history of coffee, ect...

Id much rather see an informative sub about coffee then another /v/circlejerk.

Not for nothing, I love pictures of coffee. What about like a photo Friday or a Monday morning pickup pics?

Puns aside, I think you should set aside a day where image only posts are allowed.

So... If you want, you can borrow this from my site "Studys Show Coffee is Good For You" its a doctor finally telling folks coffee IS NOT BAD.

Found it in the obscure corners of youtube.
I think everybody makes and takes their coffee a little differently. Ranging from the everyday Joe to the obsessive. I'm here to see how everybody else does coffee.

During the growth period, I'm all for relevant content...discussion, pictures, questions, etc.

my two lincolns...There's always an opportunity to splinter off at a later date if there's a need.

To clarify what I mean by content and info-dense: no image-only posts, discussion-oriented, lots of questions.

This is exactly what I'd like to see, and what usually constitutes a good verse. Image posting leads to fluffy memey content. It also doesn't automatically imply snobbery. You can have good, intelligent discussion without being snobby about it. Honestly /r/coffee is a really good sub and it wouldn't be a bad idea to try and emulate it.

One thing I'd like to plead is that /v/coffee doesn't become as snobby and self-serving as /r/coffee, because I personally feel as though the atmosphere became really off-putting there.

Often times, "advice" that was never asked for was given, there was this arrogance surrounding the advice as well. I get it, we all love coffee and we want to share that love with other people - but we need to remain open and understanding of the idea that not everyone will be as far along the path as we are.

We each took a journey to get to where we are in our currently relationship with coffee, and forcing others to take the same journey we did, the way we want them to, is off-putting. We need to accept that others may simply want a drip machine when they ask "What is the best drip machine I can get for $75", rather than telling them that a drip machine is "horrible" or that they should really be spending their money on a grinder, etc.

Let's try to answer people's questions first, and then possibly give our own advice second - but in the more pleasant way possible. Too many times I saw questions remain completely unanswered in lieu of giving someone the information we saw fit instead - it became such an arrogant circle jerk that I had to quit lurking, despite the information being high quality.

I know that comes off negative, and I talked in circles to some degree, but I hope you understand the idea I'm trying to convey.
